items.title: The Moderna cancer vaccine offers hope — now we must speed up personalized therapies
items.summary: A positive trial holds promise for treating people with cancer. More research is needed to get effective vaccines to the clinic.

items.title: The Roman telescope is about to take planet-hunting to the next level
items.summary: NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, set to launch shortly, could find 40 times the number of distant worlds that have been detected so far.

items.title: Automated prototyping of genetic codes
items.summary: A robotic, cell–free platform rapidly prototypes redesigned genetic codes, enabling the translation of proteins with reassigned codons and non-standard amino acids without altering living genomes.

items.title: Cell-type-specific eQTLs underlie the genetic architecture of complex traits
items.summary: Single-cell RNA-sequencing shows that cell-type-specific expression quantitative trait loci drive much of complex trait heritability, highlighting cell-type-specific gene regulation as key to linking genetic variants with traits.

items.title: A binding-to-release strategy for targeted anticancer drug delivery
items.summary: A binding-to-release drug conjugate strategy enables targeted payload release without cellular internalization, improving tumour specificity, efficacy and expanding therapeutic targets beyond conventional drug conjugates.

items.title: Long-read sequencing reveals pre-meiotic gene conversion in sperm
items.summary: Single-molecule long-read sequencing of human sperm reveals variation in recombination across donors and that a substantial fraction of non-crossover gene conversions arises before meiosis, distinct from PRDM9-driven recombination and associated with fragile sites.

items.title: The baffling science of SSRIs: how do they really work?
items.summary: The world’s most popular antidepressant drugs are under fire. But are they really harder to quit than heroin?

items.title: Briefing Chat: How Dolly Parton left her mark on science
items.summary: Nature reporters discuss the country-music icon's advocacy for vaccines and public health — plus, promising trial results for an mRNA cancer therapy.

items.title: A solution to the mystery of the missing neutrinos
items.summary: Lecture preparations prompt a scientist to poke holes in the ‘gallium anomaly’.

items.title: Glacier collapse caused Nepal’s deadly flash flood — a sign of things to come?
items.summary: Global warming is making high-altitude regions unstable, and could trigger more frequent landslides and floods.

items.title: Why are El Niños getting stronger? 1,000-year-coral record points to climate change
items.summary: A reconstruction of Pacific Ocean sea surface temperatures adds to the evidence that human-caused warming is boosting El Niño events.

items.title: Insights into longevity and virus-driven adaptation from Myotis bat genomes
items.summary: Comparative and functional analyses of Myotis bats uncover unique patterns of adaptation in virus-interacting proteins and longevity-associated pathways, linking two hallmarks of bat biology.

items.title: Ultrafast and reference-free sequence discovery in single-cell data
items.summary: Malva enables ultrafast, reference-free searching of raw single-cell sequences across millions of cells, transforming static transcriptomic atlases into dynamic resources for understanding the functions of sequences.

items.title: Aberrant excitatory neuronal ERBB4 promotes Alzheimer’s disease pathology
items.summary: Neuroinflammation alone may be dispensable for early synapse loss in Alzheimer’s disease.

items.title: Endocannabinoids facilitate reward engagement through retrograde gain control
items.summary: A key role for retrograde neuromodulatory signalling in motivated behaviour is shown through dynamic endocannabinoid release within a thalamostriatal circuit that regulates behavioural engagement during reward seeking.

items.title: Granule cells reorient cortical trajectories to separate contexts
items.summary: Simultaneous imaging of premotor cortex and cerebellar granule cells in mice learning two skills in parallel shows that trajectories generalize in cortex but coherently reorient apart in granule cells, supporting generalization and separation between contexts.

items.title: Plasma-jet movie is astronomy’s summer blockbuster
items.summary: Just 116 images exist of the active galaxy 3C 345 — but an AI-driven algorithm has created a highly detailed video of the plasma jets blasted from its centre.

items.title: This pulsating muscle graft mimics benefits of exercise
items.summary: Mice with the surgical implant developed more muscle mass, strength and bone density.

items.title: Vaporization trick enables ‘tandem’ solar cells to be made at lower temperatures
items.summary: A clever approach for evaporating a compound used to make perovskite semiconductors tackles a vexing challenge in scaling up next-generation solar cells.

items.title: Animal-microbe partnerships date back to the dawn of complex life
items.summary: Geochemical clues hint that worm-like creatures in the Ediacaran period benefited from symbiosis with bacteria.

items.title: ‘Robot Olympics’ reveal humanoids’ rapid progress — and flaws
items.summary: Humanoid robots broke records at sporting events such as sprints, but struggled at practical tasks such as hammering nails.

items.title: Highest-ever ocean temperatures recorded as El Niño intensifies
items.summary: Why extreme temperatures are expected to weaken ocean carbon sinks — plus, how mitochondrial injections could treat vision loss.

items.title: Amphibious stem-insect sheds light on colonization of land
items.summary: Restudy of a challenging fossil using cross-polarized light imaging and phylogenetic reconstruction identifies Chosha praecursor, a probable early-diverging insect, helping to bridge the longstanding ‘hexapod gap’ in the fossil record.

items.title: Tidal tomography reveals a thermal anomaly beneath Mars’s crustal dichotomy
items.summary: Analysis of tracking data from Mars orbiters reveals time-variable gravity field behaviour reflecting the structure underlying the Martian crustal dichotomy and indicates the preservation of a 200–400 °C thermal anomaly in the present-day mantle below the southern highlands.

items.title: Video reconstruction of variable VLBI observations with neural fields
items.summary: The kine neural reconstruction algorithm produces high-resolution, time-continuous very long baseline interferometry videos, enabling direct measurement of instantaneous plasma velocities and detailed kinematic analysis of relativistic astrophysical jets.

items.title: Infrared absorption spectroscopy of a single polyatomic molecular ion
items.summary: Non-destructive single-molecule absorption spectroscopy is achieved by detecting photon recoil from a trapped molecular ion, enabling single-photon-sensitive measurements of molecular vibrational transitions.

items.title: Smaller reactors bring nuclear power closer to fulfilling its promise
items.summary: Shadowed by past disasters, nuclear engineers are developing different types of reactor, fuel, coolant and material that could help to make fission the zero-carbon energy technology of choice.

items.title: The 46 companies scrambling to commercialize fusion for energy
items.summary: Whether the billions of dollars of investment will lead to an inexhaustible source of clean electrical power is not yet known.

items.title: Savannah grass growth in dry conditions is boosted by increased CO<sub>2</sub> levels
items.summary: Analysis of 70 experiments and 32 years of field observations shows that increasing the amount of carbon dioxide enhances the growth of the C4 group of grasses when water is limited. These findings challenge the assumption that C4 grasses respond weakly to changes in carbon dioxide level, and reveal an overlooked driver of change across the world’s savannahs.

items.title: Using nuclear waste to power space missions
items.summary: Researchers plan to use radioactive isotopes to power systems on a future Mars rover.

items.title: 3D bulk-resolved g-wave altermagnetic order parameter in CrSb
items.summary: Quantum oscillation measurements map the g-wave altermagnetic order parameter in CrSb, establishing it as a prototypical unconventional magnet with momentum-dependent spin splitting.

items.title: Synergistic degradation of fucoidans in the ocean
items.summary: Efficient degradation of fucoidans depends on complementary bacterial guilds that cooperatively break backbone and side-chain sugars, revealing a conserved, globally relevant mechanism that shapes marine carbon cycling.

items.title: Primate-specific regulation of the human glycosphingolipid gatekeeper UGCG
items.summary: Cryogenic electron microscopy structures of full-length human UGCG, the gatekeeper that dictates the scale and composition of glycosphingolipid diversity, are reported, showing that it uses a metal-independent catalytic mechanism driven by an arginine network.

items.title: Can nuclear reactors hit the road?
items.summary: Fission facilities that fit in a truck could provide portable power where it’s needed — but some people question whether it’s worth the cost, safety compromises and the risk of sending the raw materials for bombs into communities.

items.title: A practical recycling strategy for making thiophosphate molecules with enzymes
items.summary: An enzymatic platform for constructing the thiophosphate molecular motif without relying on large amounts of expensive reagents has been developed. The method lays the foundation for developing enzymatic cascades to synthesize thiophosphate-containing motifs in drug development.

items.title: Dolly Parton dies aged 80 — researchers celebrate her contributions to science
items.summary: The country singer was an advocate for vaccines, public health, literacy and marginalized communities.

items.title: A raft of start-up firms is betting on nuclear fusion
items.summary: The phenomenon that makes stars shine and hydrogen bombs explode has yet to be reliably tamed for energy generation. But that isn’t stopping companies from trying.

items.title: Will Meta’s deal make social media safe for kids? Researchers are dubious
items.summary: Nature talks to specialists about the changes coming to Facebook and Instagram, and whether there’s evidence they will help.

items.title: Systems vaccinology and the architecture of human immunity
items.summary: A review of the current state of the field of systems vaccinology discusses the challenges in translating insights into clinical and regulatory practice.

items.title: Spontaneously charged water drops induce corrosion
items.summary: Experiments have shown that spontaneously charged water drops can damage coatings on metal surfaces, leading to corrosion of the metal.

items.title: The push to clear nuclear power’s waste-disposal hurdle
items.summary: The technical issues have mostly been solved, but the long-term potential peril of radioactive material has made it difficult to find politically acceptable sites.

items.title: Heisuke Hironaka obituary: mathematician who smoothed out geometry’s complexities
items.summary: His awe-inspiring proof for the resolution of singularities — such as peaks, edges and self-crossings — revolutionized algebraic geometry.

items.title: Women face bans on research underground — here’s how to modernize the system
items.summary: In many countries, female engineers are barred from entering deep mines to carry out studies. Differentiating risks can increase access while protecting safety.

items.title: Critical zone processes limit alkalinity export from natural basaltic systems
items.summary: Observations from natural volcanic watersheds demonstrate attenuation of alkalinity fluxes along the complete reactive pathways from soil to river that lead to reductions in exported alkalinity, indicating the limiting effects of critical zone processes.

items.title: Are pro-nuclear politics a threat to public safety?
items.summary: Oversight agencies suddenly face pressure to rapidly assess a range of relatively untested reactor designs.

items.title: South Africa’s ‘registration law’ for scientists could be a template for the world — if the nation gets it right
items.summary: The plan to force some scientists to register with a professional body could protect people and the environment, but the current version lacks clarity.

items.title: What employers are looking for in the age of AI — and four ways to provide it
items.summary: For applicants whose knowledge of AI stops at the name ChatGPT, Nature spoke to academics, employers and early-career researchers to find out what you need to expand your understanding.

items.title: Daily briefing: Celebrating Dolly Parton’s contributions to science
items.summary: Parton helped to fund Moderna’s early-stage vaccine research, among other philanthropic projects. Plus, causes and treatments for depression, and how AI-detection tools are pushing back against slop.

items.title: Mysteries of the deep and AI friendship: Books in brief
items.summary: Andrew Robinson reviews five of the best science picks.

items.title: Like coffee and ice cream: an interview with Sam and Eli Morten
items.summary: Joint operation.
